text: In software development, testing plays a crucial role in ensuring quality and reliability. Unit tests check individual components, like a single function, to confirm they work correctly in isolation. Integration tests go a step further, verifying that different parts of the system interact smoothly together. Many developers use test-driven development (TDD), where they write failing tests first, then code to pass them. This approach builds confidence gradually, as each test acts as a safety net for changes. When developers add new features or fix bugs, a well-tested codebase helps prevent unexpected problems, making the software more stable and easier to maintain over time.
